chunks: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: 'The Nāsib (enemy of Ahl al-Bayt) for us, the People of the House, does not care whether he fasts or prays or commits fornication or steals; indeed, he is in the Fire.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt, the People of the House (Prophet's family)
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Al-Sadiq (The Truthful), title of Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him)
key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: An-Nasib, one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.لَا يُبَالِي: La yubali, does not care / is indifferent

ai.seo_question: What is the status of the Nāsib in Shia theology regarding their acts of worship?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) emphasizes that *Nasb* (active enmity or opposition) towards the Ahl al-Bayt is a fundamental defect that nullifies the spiritual value of outward worship, rendering the individual destined for Hellfire regardless of their ritual observance or even major sins. This highlights the Shia theological principle that correct *Wilayah* (divine authority) is the root of faith, while enmity towards the Prophet's family is the root of disbelief, superseding individual acts of devotion.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 18.  It  is  narrated  that  Imam  Muhammad  Baqir  (a.s.)  said, “For the enemies of Ahle Bayt (a.s.) there is no difference whether they observe fast and offer prayers or they commit fornication and theft. In any case they are destined to Hell and  they shall go to Hell.”
